alternatives.argument: The local definition constructs a finite balanced tree from the ordered nonempty index set and states diameter, distance, admissibility, and the deterministic one-side split.
The local definition assigns dense arrays to near leaves and finite rank-capped factors to admissible leaves; it explicitly makes low rank an input assumption.

The local proof first assembles residual blocks with disjoint entry support to obtain the root-sum-square Frobenius bound. It then uses the explicit product perturbation expansion and proves Frobenius submultiplicativity entrywise by Cauchy–Schwarz.

owner_metadata_history.reason: Actual recursive error properties now belong to the proved ordinary recompression lemma, with the procedure unchanged; scope16-algorithm-property-separation.md.

alternatives.argument: The local procedure computes each represented dense or factorized leaf action and accumulates the disjoint column-slice contribution into the matching row coordinates.
The local procedure adds near blocks densely and exactly and applies the proved bottom-up core-SVD routine to a finite factor-sum tree for each far block.

The local algorithm partitions the intermediate index set, writes each exact product term in matching factor form, and compresses a finite sum tree. Its error budget is proved by the bottom-up tail recurrence.
The local postorder recurrence represents each exact subtree sum, records the exact core-SVD tail at each node, and proves by induction that the sum of node tails bounds the root Frobenius residual.

The local theorem combines the certified disjoint-block factor errors, expands LU-Lhat Uhat into two terms, bounds the Frobenius and spectral residuals, and proves injectivity/surjectivity and the inverse bound under ||A^-1||2 eta<1.
The local proof multiplies out the finite geometric series, writes every summand as an outer product, bounds the remainder entrywise, then sums the squared entry bounds.
The local diagonal example checks the original sum is positive definite, verifies each rank-zero update error equals 3/50, and evaluates the truncated quadratic form at e2 to obtain -1/50.
The local example computes dist(tau,tau)=0 and uses the two singular values of I2 to prove every rank-one approximation has spectral error at least one.
The finite example multiplies out the rank-one factors and computes the exact 2-by-2 residual Frobenius norm.
